Hi everyone! I'm Marcin Bugaj. I've been learning Lean 4 and Mathlib, with a focus on inequalities and majorization theory. I just opened my first PR, https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/41898 - the majorization preorder on Fin n → ℝ and its T-transform (Robin Hood) decomposition.

Muirhead's inequality is ready too and will follow as a dependent PR on top of this one. Further ahead I also plan to add other characterizations of majorization - in particular via convex functions (Karamata's inequality) and related results on convex functions.

As it's my first contribution, I'd really appreciate feedback, including on file placement (Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Majorization.lean), naming (Majorizes, ≺, TTransform), and whether the ≺ notation should stay scoped. Thanks!

Hello :wave:
Did you use AI in the making of this PR? If so, can you elaborate on how exactly, per the contribution guidelines? (#use-of-ai)

The use of AI was limited to:

  • using https://leansearch.net/ to find theorems
  • using Claude Opus 4.8 to do initial research on the relevant modules and data structures (representation of a sequence, permutation etc)
  • using Claude Opus 4.8 to rename terms to match the naming convention
  • using Claude Opus 4.8 to get suggestion on how to simplify the code in some places - for instance here: https://github.com/marcinbugaj/mathlib4/blob/8ea9c322a0c8b7ee3fac3ae85998893262ca943c/Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Majorization.lean#L501-L504 - the case split without nested rcases

Other than this all code has been hand crafted by me.

I reposted that information in the PR as well.
